claim_boundary: Checked-in fixtures exercise the evaluator only. They do not measure a model and cannot support a framework-improvement claim.

cases.request: Answer in at most two compact sentences: Did the corpus build succeed, and what remains?
facts: The corpus build succeeded.
Direct paper linkage is 88 of the 100-paper target.
Twelve papers remain to reach the target.
cases.evidence_boundary: State only the supplied build result and coverage gap. Do not call the entire project complete.

visual_oracle.rationale: Two scalar facts are clearer as two sentences than as a display.

machine_checks.message: Lead with the direct build result.

machine_checks.pattern: all (?:work|coverage|the work) is complete|nothing remains|fully complete
machine_checks.message: Do not report the full project as complete.
Do not add headings to a two-sentence answer.
Do not add a table for two scalar facts.
Do not add an image to this short answer.

cases.request: Give the final engineering handoff after the parser change and the late integration-test failure.
facts: The parser change was implemented in parser.py.
All 42 unit tests passed.
The final integration test exited with status 1 because the registry credential was rejected.
The work is not complete until the integration test can run successfully.
The next action is to renew the registry credential and rerun the integration test.
cases.evidence_boundary: Report the successful unit evidence and the later blocking failure. Do not let the earlier success overwrite the final state.

visual_oracle.rationale: A compact handoff communicates this single change and blocker without a visual.

machine_checks.message: Make the final blocked state explicit.
Report the late integration-test failure and status.
Report the credential blocker or its next action.
Do not erase the late integration failure.
Do not add a decorative image.
Do not leave handoff placeholders unresolved.

cases.request: Present the benchmark in one self-contained quantitative table and give a calibrated conclusion about the accuracy/latency trade-off.
facts: Accuracy is higher-is-better and is reported as mean plus or minus standard deviation over five seeds.
Method A accuracy is 72.4 plus or minus 1.1 percent and latency is 31 milliseconds.
Method B accuracy is 74.0 plus or minus 1.0 percent and latency is 38 milliseconds.
Method C accuracy is 73.9 plus or minus 0.9 percent and latency is 29 milliseconds.
Latency is lower-is-better.
No significance test was run, so B and C cannot be declared statistically different.
cases.evidence_boundary: Describe observed means and the accuracy/latency trade-off. Do not claim statistical significance, causality, or a universal winner.

visual_oracle.rationale: Three methods on two metrics are most accurately compared in one compact table.

machine_checks.message: Present the quantitative comparison in a table.
State that significance was not tested.
Do not claim an untested significant difference.

cases.request: Show the supplied curve and report the visible late-training anomaly without inventing its cause.
facts: The mean return rises through step 80 and drops at step 90.
The shaded band denotes one standard deviation over five seeds.
The plot alone cannot identify the cause of the drop.
cases.evidence_boundary: Describe only the visible trend, aggregation, and causal limitation. The figure does not diagnose an implementation or hardware cause.

visual_oracle.rationale: The temporal trend and localized drop are materially easier to inspect in the supplied curve.

machine_checks.message: Embed the supplied local figure with nonempty alt text.
Give the figure a visible caption.
State that the cause cannot be inferred from the figure.

cases.request: Present the three protocol groups as compact tables and explain why they must not be globally ranked.
facts: Simulation protocol S reports success rate: Alpha 82 percent and Beta 79 percent.
Real-robot protocol R reports success rate: Gamma 61 percent and Delta 64 percent.
Efficiency protocol E reports latency: Alpha 32 milliseconds and Gamma 41 milliseconds; the other methods were not reported.
The protocols use different tasks and evaluation conditions and are not directly comparable.
An em dash denotes not reported, not zero.
cases.evidence_boundary: Preserve protocol grouping and units. Do not combine the groups into an overall leaderboard or treat missing values as zero.

visual_oracle.rationale: Separate tables make the incompatible protocols and their different metrics explicit.

machine_checks.message: Use separate tables for incompatible protocol groups.
Do not fragment the three protocol groups further.

machine_checks.pattern: not directly comparable|cannot be (?:globally |directly )?ranked|must not be (?:globally )?ranked
(?:em dash|—).*(?:not reported|does not mean zero)|not reported.*(?:not zero|rather than zero)
overall winner|ranks? first overall|best method overall
machine_checks.message: Do not create a global ranking.

cases.request: Summarize the synthetic paper's problem, method, main evidence, and limitations in a compact academic synthesis using only citation [P1].
facts: LatentPlan addresses model-based control with an action-conditioned latent transition model.
It is evaluated on two simulated control benchmarks.
Its mean return is 4.1 points above a behavioral-cloning baseline over three seeds.
No statistical significance test or real-robot experiment is reported.
Only source [P1] is supplied.
cases.evidence_boundary: Use only [P1]. Do not infer state of the art, statistical significance, real-robot validation, or broader generalization.

visual_oracle.rationale: A four-part synthesis of one paper does not need a display.

machine_checks.message: Preserve the mean gain and seed count.

machine_checks.pattern: no (?:statistical )?significance test.*no real[- ]robot|no real[- ]robot.*no (?:statistical )?significance test|neither.*significance.*nor.*real[- ]robot|(?:absence|lack) of (?:a )?(?:statistical )?significance test.*(?:and|,).*?(?:a )?real[- ]robot experiment|no (?:statistical )?significance test (?:or|and) (?:a )?real[- ]robot experiment

machine_checks.message: Do not invent a ranking claim.
Do not add a decorative image.

cases.request: Give a current incident update after the failed deployment and rollback.
facts: The new deployment failed with HTTP 401.
Rollback to the previous version succeeded and user traffic is healthy.
The new version is not deployed.
A rotated credential is a suspected cause, but the root cause is unverified.
The incident remains blocked pending credential validation and a safe redeploy.
cases.evidence_boundary: Separate service recovery from incident resolution. Do not present the suspected credential cause as confirmed.

visual_oracle.rationale: One failed deployment and rollback can be communicated more directly in prose.

machine_checks.message: Lead with the blocked current state.
Report rollback and current user impact.

machine_checks.pattern: new version (?:is )?not deployed|deployment of the new version remains blocked
machine_checks.message: State that the new version is not deployed.

machine_checks.pattern: credential.*suspect.*(?:unverified|not confirmed|not yet confirmed)|suspect.*credential.*(?:unverified|not confirmed|not yet confirmed)

machine_checks.message: Do not confuse rollback with resolution.
Do not add a decorative incident image.

cases.request: Report the ablation of the gated diffusion policy: remove the gate, the noise schedule, and the data augmentation one at a time, and state what each component contributes.
facts: Success is higher-is-better and is reported as mean success percent with standard deviation over five seeds, 200 scenes per seed.
Full system: 84.2 percent success, standard deviation 1.9 points.
Without gate: 76.5 percent, standard deviation 2.4 points.
Without noise schedule: 82.9 percent, standard deviation 2.1 points.
Without data augmentation: 80.1 percent, standard deviation 2.6 points.
Every variant was tuned with the same 12-trial budget as the full system.
Removing the gate and the augmentation together was not run.
No significance test was run.
cases.evidence_boundary: Attribute contributions only as observed drops from the full system under the shared tuning budget. Do not claim the components are independent or additive, and do not claim significance because no test was run.

visual_oracle.rationale: Four variants on one metric with uncertainty read fastest as one table with the full system as the reference row.

machine_checks.message: Present the variants in a table with the full system as the reference row.
State that every variant received the same tuning budget.
State that the untested combination blocks any additivity or independence claim.
Do not claim an untested significant difference.
Do not claim the component effects add up; the joint removal was not run.

cases.request: Write up the benchmarking study of the new inference kernel against the tuned baseline: report throughput and tail latency across the four batch sizes and give the speedup honestly.
facts: Batch sizes tested: 1, 8, 32, 128. Timings are the median of 20 runs after 5 warm-up runs on one A100 80GB with CUDA 12.4, kernel v2.1 versus baseline v1.9.
Throughput speedup over the baseline: 1.12x at batch 1, 1.35x at batch 8, 2.40x at batch 32, 3.10x at batch 128.
Geometric mean speedup across the four batch sizes is 1.83x.
p99 latency at batch 1 rose from 4.1 ms to 4.6 ms; at every other batch size p99 fell.
The baseline was retuned for this hardware and measured 8 percent faster than its published numbers.
cases.evidence_boundary: Report the best-case speedup only next to the geometric mean and the worst case. Do not present 3.1x as the headline alone, and disclose the batch-1 tail-latency regression and the hardware and software stack.

visual_oracle.rationale: Four batch sizes on two metrics fit one compact table; four points do not need a chart.

machine_checks.message: Present the per-batch results in a table.
Report the geometric-mean speedup next to any best case.
Never state up to 3.1x without the geometric mean or worst case in the same breath.
Disclose the repetition and warm-up protocol.
Disclose that the baseline was retuned and how it compares with its published numbers.
